source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: vendor master record, including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoice uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The only safeguard against an unsafe payment or bank change is the model's own decision to request approval and what it chooses to put in the one-line summary. Nothing structural forces the summary to disclose that a bank detail change occurred or to show the account number itself.

No amount threshold, vendor allowlist, or scope limit is defined. The agent can update bank details and schedule payment for any vendor an invoice claims to match, using a credential that is not scoped per vendor.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The gate is enforced in orchestration (the action blocks pending a human click), so it does not vanish with model capability. But the clerk sees only a model-generated one-line summary, never the raw bank account number or change history (runtime notes), so a more persuasive or selectively incomplete model summary defeats it without any technical bypass. Classified per control_decay.md 'Human approval gate, model summary review'.

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of vendor bank detail changes
controls.decay_rationale: Verifying a bank change through a channel the invoice sender cannot control (for example, calling a phone number already on file, not one in the invoice) is enforced outside the model and outside the attacker's reach, so it does not decay as the model gets more capable.

controls.name: Show raw bank account diff and change history in the approval card
controls.decay_rationale: If the old/new account numbers and change flag are populated directly from the system of record rather than authored by the model, the approver's view does not depend on the model choosing to disclose them. This would move approval_review_mode from model_summary to raw_action.

controls.name: Scope the ERP credential to the vendor matched on the current invoice
controls.decay_rationale: A credential narrowed to the vendor and PO matched on the current invoice does not depend on model behavior; it bounds blast radius structurally.

findings.title: TC9: Summary-gated irreversible payment to a fraudulently updated bank account via untrusted invoice data

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled invoice uploaded to the supplier portal claims new bank details for the vendor.
Agent updates the vendor's bank details based solely on invoice content.
Bank-change approval card shows only a one-line summary; the clerk is never shown the account number or that this is a change, so cannot detect fraud.
Agent schedules payment on the due date to the now-fraudulent account.
Payment approval card shows payee, amount, invoice id, and PO match, but does not mention that a bank change occurred for this vendor.

findings.residual_rationale: Crediting ctl.clerk_approval (structural, partially_dependent, model_summary) per rubric step 2 floors residual at moderate (critical minus two tiers). Residual is rated high instead because the runtime notes state bank account numbers and change history are never shown to the clerk under any circumstance: this is a permanent structural blind spot the clerk cannot close by being more careful, not merely a summarization risk a cautious model might mitigate. The gate therefore provides materially less protection than the moderate floor assumes.

forecast.watch_signal: Platform model version string changes (subject.model.swappable is true, so upgrades ship with no separate review); clerk approval clickthrough rate rising above the current ~150/day; or the approval step being disabled or narrowed in runtime config.

evidence.observation: "If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record" - the agent treats untrusted invoice content as authoritative for a sensitive vendor-master change.
"Before any payment or bank change, request approval with a one line summary so the clerk can approve quickly" - the only safeguard is a human gate driven by a model-authored one-line summary.
The shown card discloses only payee, amount, invoice id, and PO match; it does not mention that a bank detail change occurred for this vendor.

"The card shows only the model's summary. Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown"; "The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day"; "The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment"; "The model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review."

recommendations.action: Require out-of-band verification (a callback to a phone number already on file, never one taken from the invoice) before applying any bank detail change.
Switch approval_review_mode to raw_action: show the clerk the actual old/new bank account numbers, and flag on the payment approval card that a bank change occurred recently for this vendor.
Scope the ERP credential used by this agent to least privilege: limit bank_update and schedule_payment to the specific vendor matched to the current invoice batch, not 'any vendor'.
Log every bank detail change with a before/after diff, route it to a second reviewer (segregation of duties), and hold the first payment to a newly changed account for a cool-down period.

findings.title: ASI03: Overbroad ERP credential lets a single invoice-driven task touch any vendor's bank and payment records

attack_path.note: Untrusted invoice content is the only input determining which vendor record the agent modifies.
Executed with an ERP credential scoped to 'any vendor', not just the one matched to this invoice, so a matching error or manipulated invoice field can redirect the write to the wrong vendor.
The same summary-only gate covers this path and does not show which vendor record was actually targeted versus the one named on the invoice.

findings.residual_rationale: Crediting ctl.clerk_approval floors residual at moderate (critical minus two tiers), but as in f1 the approver can never see the bank account data needed to catch a wrong-vendor or mismatched update, and no credential-scoping control exists to bound the blast radius to the matched vendor. Rated high rather than the computed floor for the same reason.

forecast.watch_signal: New vendor data sources or integrations added (data_scope_expansion), or the model upgraded while no credential-scoping control has been added.

evidence.observation: "The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment" - no scoping to the vendor matched on the current invoice.
"Match each invoice to a vendor and purchase order" - vendor targeting is performed by the model's own matching logic, not enforced by the credential.

recommendations.action: Issue a narrowly scoped, per-task credential (or attribute-based access control) so the agent can only write to the vendor record matched to the invoice it is currently processing.
Alert when a bank_update or schedule_payment call targets a vendor other than the one named on the invoice being processed in the same task.

rating.rationale: Both findings start at critical: an untrusted, attacker-authored invoice can drive an irreversible external payment and a confidential vendor-record write through a broadly scoped ERP credential, with no declared step or runtime bounds, which triggers the autonomy modifier. The only preventive control, ctl.clerk_approval, is structural but partially_dependent because it operates in model_summary mode, and it is further undermined by a hardcoded data blackout: the clerk never sees the bank account number or change history under any circumstance. That pushes residual to high rather than the rubric's moderate floor for a typical summary gate. Under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, or control_removal, control_decay.md predicts this summary-review gate fails first; with the agent's model already set to upgrade with the platform and no separate review (subject.model.swappable = true), there is no decay buffer left, so forecast returns to critical.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design in prompt.md, the approval card sample, and the runtime notes provided; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or source code was supplied, so capability scope (exact credential_scope and action semantics for erp.update_vendor_bank_details and erp.schedule_payment) is inferred from prose rather than verified configuration.
No data was provided on invoice volume, typical payment amount, or any existing vendor-onboarding verification process, which would refine the likelihood and consequence ratings.
